text:
maria: hi team 👋 finishing my mac M2 bootstrap. hit a couple small annoyances: asdf python install fails, and npm global installs complain about permissions. anyone seen this combo?

ben: welcome! share the errors?

maria: asdf: 
```
$ asdf install python 3.11.4
Downloading Python-3.11.4.tar.xz...
configure: error: cannot find zlib
```

maria: npm error when installing a global tool: `Error: EACCES: permission denied, access '/usr/local/lib/node_modules'`

ryan: install zlib dev libs: `brew install zlib openssl sqlite3 xz` then set env before build, e.g. `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix zlib)/lib"; export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix zlib)/include"` and retry asdf python. For ASDF+Homebrew on M1/M2 we add these to `~/.asdf/plugins/python/env` in our dotfiles.

ryan: for npm globals on mac, we recommend configuring npm to user space: `mkdir -p ~/.npm-global && npm config set prefix '~/.npm-global'` and add `export PATH=~/.npm-global/bin:$PATH` to your shell rc. We avoid sudo for npm.

maria: thanks. small follow-up: my dotfiles repo uses an SSH submodule for private configs and git clone prompts for passphrase every time. can I use 1password CLI to load SSH key?

ben: yes — install `op` CLI, then `eval $(op signin)` and `op item get "redwood-ssh" --fields sshkey | gpg --decrypt > ~/.ssh/id_rsa && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/id_rsa`. We actually store keys in 1Password and a post-bootstrap job rotates them. If you want, ping security for a short key-rotation session.

maria: perfect, I already had `op` from the onboarding list. last tiny gotcha: direnv complains about `.envrc` not allowed in some repos.

ryan: run `direnv allow` once per repo. We also keep a repo-level `.envrc` in the infra repos that sources a central `.envrc_shared` so CI whitelists it.

maria: all green now, thanks both! happy to help update the onboarding checklist with the zlib/nvm/npm notes if useful.
